architectures.name: Implantable drug reservoir + micro-pump
architectures.mechanism: Implanted drug reservoir connected to eShunt; micro-pump delivers bolus drug doses into CSF on schedule or sensor-triggered
architectures.operating_state: Pump delivers drug at programmed intervals; reservoir refillable via transcutaneous port
architectures.failure_state: Pump failure → no drug delivery (CSF drainage continues via shunt)
architectures.emergency_state: Reservoir leak → drug dump into CSF (dose-limiting design prevents toxicity)
architectures.manufacturing_concept: Titanium reservoir + MEMS micro-pump + catheter integration
architectures.regulatory_implications: Combination product (device + drug); requires drug-specific clinical trial
architectures.potential_claim_territory: Endovascular CSF shunt with integrated drug delivery pump

architectures.name: Coated eShunt with drug-eluting surface
architectures.mechanism: eShunt inner lumen coated with drug-eluting polymer; drug releases continuously into CSF as it flows past
architectures.operating_state: Sustained drug release over weeks/months; coating degrades safely
architectures.failure_state: Coating delamination → burst release or no release
architectures.emergency_state: All coating releases at once → drug toxicity (dose-limiting coating design)
architectures.manufacturing_concept: Dip-coat or spray-coat eShunt with drug-polymer matrix
architectures.regulatory_implications: Combination product; drug-specific; coating must demonstrate controlled release
architectures.potential_claim_territory: Endovascular CSF shunt with drug-eluting coating

architectures.name: Dual-lumen eShunt (drainage + drug delivery)
architectures.mechanism: Two-lumen catheter: one lumen drains CSF, second lumen delivers drug from external pump or implanted reservoir
architectures.operating_state: Independent drainage and drug delivery; no interference between flows
architectures.failure_state: Drug lumen occlusion → no drug delivery (drainage unaffected)
architectures.emergency_state: Lumen cross-leak → drug enters drainage (dose-limiting valve prevents overdose)
architectures.manufacturing_concept: Co-extruded dual-lumen catheter; drug lumen smaller diameter
architectures.regulatory_implications: Combination product; simpler than ARCH-001 (no implanted pump)
architectures.potential_claim_territory: Dual-lumen endovascular CSF shunt with drug delivery lumen

architectures.name: Pressure-activated drug release
architectures.mechanism: Drug reservoir with pressure-activated valve; releases drug when ICP rises above threshold (combining Position 2 monitoring with drug delivery)
architectures.operating_state: Drug releases only when ICP elevated; closed-loop feedback
architectures.failure_state: Valve failure → no release or continuous release
architectures.emergency_state: Valve stuck open → drug dump (dose-limiting reservoir design)
architectures.manufacturing_concept: Spring-loaded valve + drug reservoir + pressure sensor
architectures.regulatory_implications: Combination product + sensor; most complex regulatory pathway
architectures.potential_claim_territory: Pressure-activated drug delivery in endovascular CSF shunt

architectures.name: Convection-enhanced delivery (CED) via eShunt
architectures.mechanism: Use eShunt anatomy to deliver drug via convection-enhanced delivery (positive pressure infusion) rather than passive diffusion
architectures.operating_state: Infusion pump maintains positive pressure; drug distributes throughout CSF
architectures.failure_state: Infusion pressure too high → CSF backflow; too low → insufficient distribution
architectures.emergency_state: Pressure runaway → CSF over-drainage (pressure-limiting valve required)
architectures.manufacturing_concept: External infusion pump + eShunt catheter modification
architectures.regulatory_implications: Combination product; CED is established technique but new in eShunt context
architectures.potential_claim_territory: Convection-enhanced drug delivery via endovascular CSF shunt
